newsitem.title: USA: Mild weather moderates N.Dakota livestock stress.
newsitem.headline: Mild weather moderates N.Dakota livestock stress.

text.p: Mild weather during the week ended Sunday helped limit stress to livestock in North Dakota, the state agricultural statistics service said Monday in a special crop weather report.

Improved weather allowed producers and road crews to get caught up on snow removal, and if mild conditions improve producers will be better able to access livestock feed and transport grain, the report said.
The state average snow depth Sunday was 17.9 inches, compared to 22.4 inches last week and 10.4 inches one year ago.
Heavy snow accumulation caused more buildings and pole barns to collapse during the week.

Livestock conditions were relatively unchanged from a week ago and were rated five percent very poor, 17 poor, 42 fair, 34 good and two percent excellent. That compared to five percent very poor, 18 poor, 41 fair, 34 good and two excellent last week.
